Subject: Post-call: Storix Health discovery — model fit recommendations, function-calling eval, next steps

Hi Alice / David —

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap + proposed next steps so we keep momentum: 

Summary of what we heard
- Primary use case: automated intake parsing and triage for patient-facing forms (structured extraction + routing). PHI will be present in samples.
- Volume: ~25k forms/month initially, peak concurrency during business hours ~40 req/s.
- Success criteria: >95% schema compliance for required fields, <250ms median token-generation latency for API path, and measurable reduction in manual triage time.

Redwood model/eval recommendations (high-level)
- Start evaluation with a quantized open model variant (we recommend LlamaX-13B-8bit and LlamaX-33B-4bit for head-to-head).
- Use structured-output + function-calling approach: primary response is a JSON payload matching your intake schema; include a human_readable summary for auditing.
- Run a small benchmark on 500 representative forms (we can bootstrap with redacted samples).

Tooling and function-calling notes (short)
- We'll provide a JSON Schema for validation and a lightweight retry policy: 2 attempts with exponential backoff on transient 5xx or model-timeout.
- KV-prefix caching for repeated question patterns is recommended to reduce cost on repeated prompts.

Immediate asks / next steps
1) Can you provide 500 de-identified (PHI redacted) sample forms or a synthetic export by Friday 4/12? If PHI cannot be redacted, we need a signed DPA + Private deployment conversation (Grace can own).
2) I'll schedule a 60-min technical deep-dive with Markus to finalize the JSON schema and function contract (propose Tue 4/16 10:00 PT).
3) We'll run an initial run and share benchmark links + a short evaluation dashboard (expected ~3 business days once data received).

Attachments included: initial prompt set template and a blank evaluation spreadsheet (attached below).

Thanks —
Kimberly Park

Hi all —

Couple of technical clarifications and a proposed concrete plan for the eval run: 

Model variants and why
- LlamaX-13B-8bit: lower cost, faster latency; good for most structured-extract tasks if schema is well-scoped.
- LlamaX-33B-4bit: higher quality for edge cases and complex free-text summaries. Use as fallback for requests failing schema validation or flagged low-confidence.

Evaluation setup (500 samples)
- Preprocess: normalize fields and remove PII (we'll share a small transformer to map common OCR noise).
- Prompting: two-shot prompt template (we include the prompt set attached) with explicit 'return EXACT JSON matching schema' instruction.
- Validation: Redwood console will run JSON Schema validation; failures get error codes: 422-schema-mismatch, 429-timeout, 502-model-error.

Function-calling & retry policy
- Function contract: single POST-able JSON blob with top-level keys: patient, form_type, fields, confidence_score, human_review_required (boolean).
- Retry rules: on 502 or 524 or internal timeout >5s, retry once after 800ms; if schema mismatch (422) do NOT retry — log and send to human_review queue.
- Confidence heuristic: if confidence_score < 0.82 send to LlamaX-33B-4bit for re-run; if still <0.82 mark for human review.

Observability and gating
- We'll enable token-level cost breakdown and schema-failure rate dashboard.
- Recommend a canary: 5% traffic on LlamaX-33B for first 48 hours post-rollout.

Estimated resource needs and rough cost for the 500-sample run
- Warm-up and runs expected to consume ~12 GPU-hours on a p4d-equivalent pool if runs are batched aggressively.
- Token estimate: ~1.2M tokens across prompts + responses; rough hosted trial cost estimate $750-$1,200 depending on batching and model choice. If Private deployment required, we will need to scope infra and licensing; Grace can own that convo.

I attached a starter JSON Schema and a sample retry-state table for the engineering team.

—Markus
Markus Klein
Principal Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
